 Central Notes: Wade, Duren, McConnell, Rivers, Lillard
 By Arthur Hill |
 at November 7, 2026 9:51 pm 
 Dean Wade was hoping to re-sign with the Cavaliers this summer, but he said the “craziness” of the offseason prevented it from happening, Chris Fedor of Cleveland.com writes in a subscriber-only piece. Wade spent seven years in Cleveland after joining the team on a two-way contract in 2019. He became a versatile member of the rotation who excelled defensively and could hit three-pointers, and he was effective both as a starter and reserve.
 Wade wanted to continue in that role, but the Cavs spent much of the summer chasing stars after reaching the Eastern Conference finals. They were rumored to be in the mix to trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo or Jaylen Brown , and they were hoping to bring back LeBron James , who didn’t announce that he was signing with Philadelphia until late July. That uncertainty meant they couldn’t commit the necessary money to keep Wade.
 “I was super comfortable with it here. I thought I’d probably just come back to Cleveland,” Wade said. “Had a house and relationships with everyone, so it would have been easy. But it just didn’t happen. It’s unfortunate.” 
 Wade called it “weird” to walk into Rocket Arena on Friday as a visitor for the first time in his career, and he and his former teammates engaged in some verbal sparring during the game. He added that things are working out well with the Sixers , as he’s surrounded by stars on one of the league’s best teams.
 “For my options that I had, made a great decision and I’m building relationships here,” Wade said. “Philly is awesome. This team is great. High-character people. Weird going to a new place and meeting like a thousand new people. But after a couple weeks, it gets a lot easier. Pretty happy with my decision.” 
 There’s more from the Central Division:
 Jalen Duren has been sidelined since October 23 with a hamstring strain , and the Pistons are clearly missing his inside presence, observes Omari Sankofa II of The Detroit Free Press (subscription required). More of the scoring is coming from beyond the arc, and they’re 28th in the league in offensive rebounding percentage after finishing second last season. Duren is nearing his two-week reevaluation of the injury.
 T.J. McConnell finished with six points, two rebounds and an assist in nine minutes on Saturday in his first game of the season, per Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star . The Pacers guard, who had been dealing with a strained right hamstring, appeared to be on a minutes restriction and wasn’t used in the second half, Dopirak adds.
 Along with the other thoughts he expressed this week on The Bill Simmons Podcast , former Bucks coach Doc Rivers said Damian Lillard “was really never welcomed in the way he should’ve been” after being acquired from Portland in a 2023 trade, relays Jim Owczarski of the Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel (subscription required). Rivers recalls that Lillard was dealing with several off-court issues at the time, including divorce proceedings. “He had a lot going on in Portland. You couldn’t have traded for him at a worse time,” Rivers said. “The biggest thing with that trade is like, you just can’t trade Jrue (Holiday) . I always thought once I got there, I said, man, if Jrue had been there with Dame and Giannis, that team would’ve been so much better.” Rivers also declined to comment on Milwaukee’s decision to waive Lillard last summer and stretch his contract through the 2029/30 season.
